## Natural history notes

A small geometrid moth characterized by grayish-brown to tan wings with angular edges, fine wavy crosslines, and bark-like mottling that helps it blend into woody stems and tree trunks. In Florida, it is found in wooded habitats such as hammocks, pine-oak woodlands, forest edges, parks, and yards where suitable host trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars are associated with plants in the cypress family and help move woody-plant foliage into the broader food web for birds, spiders, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
